coolflames.title: Low-Temperature 'Cool Flames' & Invisible Microgravity Hazards
coolflames.content:
During the Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX & FLEX-2, PSI-69) and Cool Flames Investigation (CFI) inside the Combustion Integrated Rack's Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA), liquid heptane and decane fuel droplets appeared to extinguish from radiative heat loss—yet the droplet continued shrinking rapidly (Nayagam et al., Combustion and Flame 2012, DOI: 10.1016/j.combustflame.2012.07.009)!

Key Findings:
• Invisible Combustion: The liquid droplet flame transitioned into a low-temperature 'cool flame' burning at only 500–800 K (compared to typical hot flames at 1500–2000 K). There was virtually no visible light emission and negligible soot.
• Chemical Pathway: Governed by low-temperature hydrocarbon peroxy-radical oxidation kinetics rather than conventional thermal chain-branching.
• Critical Safety Hazard: An astronaut could believe a fire is completely out while cool flame combustion silently continues. Introducing a fresh ventilation draft can trigger sudden, explosive hot re-ignition without warning.
• Evidence Boundary: Droplet burning and cool flame persistence in FLEX demonstrate liquid fuel phase-change and low-temperature kinetics, strictly distinct from gaseous diffusion flames on porous spherical burners (ACME s-Flame).

saffire.title: Saffire I–VI: Large-Scale Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstrations
saffire.content:
NASA's Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration (Saffire) addressed the ultimate question: How does a real, large-scale structural fire behave inside an actual spacecraft module?

Key Findings:
• Scale Matters: Prior glovebox experiments were restricted to small samples (<10 cm). Saffire burned massive 1.0 m x 0.4 m fabric panels (cotton/fiberglass blends and PMMA acrylic) inside Cygnus cargo vehicles after departing the ISS.
• Flame Growth: Upward/downward flame spread in low-speed forced ventilation (10–30 cm/s) does not self-extinguish. The flame establishes a wide, creeping pyrolysis front that rapidly consumes available oxygen while producing dense toxic CO and smoke.
• Cabin Pressure Transients: Large fires cause localized thermal expansion and pressure spikes that can overwhelm life support relief valves before the fire exhausts itself.

cir.title: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) & Multi-user Apparatus (MDCA)
cir.content:
The Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) is NASA's flagship microgravity combustion research facility on the ISS, managed by NASA Glenn Research Center.

Key Capabilities:
• 100-liter sealed combustion chamber with diagnostic optics and mass flow controllers.
• Hosted two major modular inserts: (a) ACME (6 gaseous flame studies: BRE, CFI-G, E-FIELD, CLD Flame, s-Flame, Flame Design) and (b) MDCA (Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus for liquid droplets in FLEX, FLEX-2, and CFI).
• Diagnostic Suite: 5 high-speed intensified cameras, PLIF laser sheet optics, chemiluminescence spectrometers, radiometers, and precision gas replenishment/scrubbing systems.

moon.title: Artemis Lunar Base Flammability & Partial-G Acceleration
moon.content:
Artemis habitats will operate at NASA's 'Exploration Atmosphere'—34% O₂ at 8.2 psi (56.5 kPa)—to mitigate astronaut decompression sickness before EVA spacewalks.

Key Risks & Scientific Clarifications:
• Flammability Explosion: 34% O₂ significantly exceeds material Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI). Materials classified as self-extinguishing on Earth (such as DuPont Nomex HT90-40, passing NASA-STD-6001B Test 1 with burn length < 15 cm / 6 in. in 21% O₂) become readily flammable in 34% O₂ Exploration Atmosphere, exceeding their conditional LOI (typically 28–30% O₂) and failing Test 1 (burn length exceeds 15 cm / 6 in.). Note that Nomex LOI is not a universal fixed constant but varies with fabric areal weight, weave, edge hemming, and moisture conditioning.
• The 1/6g Penalty: In 0.16g, buoyant convection is too weak to create strong convective cooling, but strong enough to supply fresh oxygen into the reaction zone. Theoretical low-buoyancy combustion models (T'ien / Ferkul 1999) predict that solid flame spread rates can peak at intermediate partial gravities (~0.15–0.3g) before dropping as 1g convective cooling takes over. In-situ flight validation awaits the Artemis FM2 / LUCI payload.
• Quiescent Microgravity Clarification: In zero-g without ventilation, flames do not automatically extinguish; molecular diffusion transport can sustain gaseous spherical diffusion flames (ACME s-Flame) or liquid droplet burning (FLEX PSI-69), governed by diffusion-to-loss ratios. Note that gaseous spherical burner flames (s-Flame) and liquid droplet combustion (FLEX) represent distinct physical combustion modes and are not interchangeable evidence.

suppress.title: Microgravity Fire Suppression Protocols & Standards Compliance
suppress.content:
Fire safety in space requires strictly distinguishing human physiological life-support atmospheres (NASA-STD-3001 Rev F, Approved July 14, 2026; superseding Rev D) from material flammability screening standards (NASA-STD-6001B):

Normative Standards & Protocols:
• Atmospheric Standards (NASA-STD-3001 Rev F):
  - [V2 6002] Inert Diluent: Requires at least 30% diluent gas (N₂), assuming the balance is oxygen.
  - [V2 6003] Inspired Oxygen (PIO₂): Calculated via Table 6.2-1 relationship PIO₂ = (PB - 47 mmHg) × FIO₂. Official Table 6.2-1 boundaries: Normoxia Target Range is 145–155 mmHg (19.3–20.7 kPa, Indefinite); Mild Hypoxia Lower Limit is 127 mmHg (16.9 kPa, Indefinite with monitoring**; 1-hour TWA; 122 mmHg absolute lower limit per Footnote ****). Artemis EAM (34% O₂ at 8.2 psia yields PIO₂ ≈ 128.2 mmHg) satisfies the 127 mmHg Mild Hypoxia Lower Limit but operates below the Normoxia Target Range, requiring active crew monitoring and operational mitigations per Table 6.2-1 Footnote **.
  - [V2 6006] Total Pressure: Strict interval 34.5 kPa < pressure ≤ 103.0 kPa (5.004 < psi ≤ 14.939 psia).
• Material Flammability Standards (NASA-STD-6001B w/Change 3, Test 1):
  - Specimen & Test Configuration: Five (5) specimens, each 30 cm × 6.5 cm (12 in × 2.5 in), tested one at a time, mounted vertically.
  - Acceptance Criteria: Burn length must not exceed 15 cm (6 in.) for any specimen, and zero flaming material transfer or drips that ignite K-10 indicator paper placed below the sample. Failure of any one specimen constitutes failure of the material in that test environment. (General failure threshold is burn length > 15 cm / 6 in. or paper ignition, not the full 30 cm coupon length; calibrated thermal energy 750 ± 50 J per Section 7.1.3.1; the 25 s ignition dwell is UNVERIFIED with no primary WSTF or NASA record produced, and is not an established standard mandate).
• Immediate Ventilation Isolation: BASS-II (PSI-25) proved that forced airflow strongly accelerates flame spread in zero-g. The primary initial response is isolating forced ventilation to starve convective transport.
• Diffusion Persistence Caution: Shutting off ventilation does not guarantee immediate extinction because diffusion flames can persist in zero-g (e.g. ACME s-Flame gaseous diffusion, FLEX liquid droplet burning); thermal IR verification is required to detect hot or low-temperature cool flames before restoring ventilation. Note that liquid droplets and gaseous burners demonstrate distinct combustion modes and are not interchangeable evidence.
• Fine Water Mist vs N₂ Inerting: Fine Water Mist (<50 µm droplets) absorbs heat through vaporization without toxic asphyxiation or post-fire cleanup hazards.
